title: Cardinal Forensics: Sample Rows Checked

callee.name: Lena Hartmann, CISO (VP Corporate Communications on speaker)
callee.label: Tallis Home Products – CISO

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: Morning, it's Renata Okafor at Cardinal, on INC-27-0309-01. Have you got a minute? I have a first read on the forum sample.

transcript.speaker: CISO
transcript.text: Go ahead. I've got our VP Corporate Communications on speaker. She's keeping the fact sheet.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: Okay. We matched 40 of the 200 sample rows against the web store export. 38 of them are real Tallis accounts. They match your records exactly. The other two don't exist anywhere. One is 'Toastina Crumbsworth, 1 Waffle Iron Way' and the other is 'Sir Blendalot, Apt 404'. That's padding. Somebody had fun.

transcript.speaker: CISO
transcript.text: So 38 of 40 are real. What's in the columns?

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: The columns are name, email, ship and bill address, phone, pwd and card. The 'pwd' values are bcrypt strings that start with dollar-two-b-dollar-twelve. They're hashes, not plain text.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: And this matters for your press people. The 'card' column isn't card numbers. It's Lakeview Payments token strings, like 'lkvp underscore tok underscore 9F3K' and so on. So the seller is calling tokens 'cards'. That's the claim in the forum title.

transcript.speaker: WRITER
transcript.text: Can we say how many accounts were taken? The post says 1.9 million.

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: No. I can't give you a count yet, and I wouldn't repeat theirs. That needs the full export logs from CartBridge, every page of every call on that integration key. Until we have those, the number is unknown. It could be smaller or larger than whatever you'd guess.

transcript.speaker: CISO
transcript.text: Understood. I'll get the log request to CartBridge in writing. When's your next update?

transcript.speaker: CARDINAL
transcript.text: As soon as the logs arrive. I'll email a written summary of this call to you in the next fifteen minutes so it's on paper.

voiceStyles.CARDINAL: Woman in her late 30s, calm and precise forensic analyst, typing faintly in the background, speaks quickly but clearly
voiceStyles.CISO: Man in his 50s, focused, short sentences, slightly tired
voiceStyles.WRITER: Woman in her 40s, careful, writing as she listens

instructorNote: Clue inject: Cardinal Forensics confirms the sample is mostly real and corrects the seller's claims about "passwords + cards", but gives no count. Check that the CISO and WRITER log time-stamped, sourced lines on the fact sheet: 38 of 40 rows are real, the count is not yet known, the data includes bcrypt-hashed passwords and payment tokens, and no full card numbers are stored. The two fake rows should be logged as attacker padding. Make sure nobody turns this into "no payment information" or quotes 1.9 million.
